paragraphs.text: Rulers and chieftains of the captives in Babylon, pretending to be far better than those elders at Jerusalem, complained about in Eze 8:11-12, but indeed no better; nay, so much the worse, because they had lost the fruit of all their afflictions, and were as arrant hypocrites as those veteratores old hands, the scribes and Pharisees, that came to John’s baptism and to our Saviour’s sermons, with evil and exulcerate minds.
paragraphs.anchor: Then came certain of the elders unto me.

paragraphs.text: “ Non omnes sancti qui calcant limina Templi. ”
A Doeg may set his foot as far within the sanctuary as a David.

Demurely and, to see to, devoutly. But why could they not stand to hear the Word of God for reverence sake? Balak did so, {Num 23:18} though a king; and Eglon, though unwieldy; {Jdg 3:20} and a better man than they both, Constantine the Great, as Eusebius {a} records, and further tells us, that being pressed, after long time of hearing, to sit down, with a stern countenance he answered, It were a great sin in me not to hear with utmost attention when God is speaking.
paragraphs.anchor: And sat before me.

paragraphs.text: {a} De Vita Const.

Lest the prophet, seeing these seniors coming thus unto him, should favour them too far, God uncaseth them, as he doth mostly such gross hypocrites in this present life; Jeroboam and his wife, Ananias and Sapphira, Simon Magus, and others for instance. How else indeed should the name of such wicked wretches rot as they must? {Pro 10:24-29}
paragraphs.anchor: And the word of the Lord came.

paragraphs.text: Though they would seem to abhor idols, yet the devil is at inn with them, and their hearts are no better than so many idol temples, as thou wouldst easily perceive hadst thou but my fiery eyes, and couldst see their insides as I do. Sustulerunt stercoreos deos suos super cor suum, {a} they have laid their dungy deities upon their very hearts; a place where I only should be by right, for it is the bridal bed.
paragraphs.anchor: These men have set their idols in their hearts.

paragraphs.text: i.e., They are impudent sinners, as the scholiast {b} interprets it, and resolved of their course whatever comes of it.
paragraphs.anchor: And put the stumblingblock of their iniquity

paragraphs.text: Should I be inquired of {c} at all by them?] q.d., No, never; I scorn the motion, I abhor such ludibrious devotion as this is. Away with it. Piscator rendereth the words, An ergo serio interrogor ab eis? Thinkest thou that I am seriously sought unto by these? q.d., Nothing less.
{a} Piscator.
{b} One who writes explanatory notes upon an author; esp. an ancient commentator upon a classical writer. ŒD
{c} Hoc significat crassum Dei contemptum et quasi professam rebellionem.
Or, As I am the Lord (oath wise), I will answer him, but with bitter answers
paragraphs.anchor: I the Lord will answer him.

paragraphs.text: i.e., As by his abominations he hath well deserved; or, concerning the multitude of his idols; that is a sin he shall be sure to hear of, and to suffer for.
paragraphs.anchor: According to the multitude of his idols

paragraphs.text: Ut deprehendam, or, as others, ut reprehendam; that I may convince their consciences of their impieties, and sting them to the heart with unquestionable conviction and horror.
paragraphs.anchor: That I may take the house of Israel in their own heart.

paragraphs.text: And fallen in with the devil, who is ειδωλοχαρης, as saith Synesius, a great promoter of idolatry. Idola sunt prima saliva, et initium deficiendi a Deo. {a} Idolatry paveth the way to utter apostasy.
paragraphs.anchor: Because they are all estranged from me.

paragraphs.text: {a} Oecolamp.
Or, Turn others; for true converts will be converting their brethren. They like not to go to heaven alone.
paragraphs.anchor: Repent, and turn yourselves.

paragraphs.text: Alii dicunt uxores vestras, saith Lavater here; your wives, which are according to your hearts, like as in water face answereth to face. Wean them from their idols, and win them over to the true God.
paragraphs.anchor: And turn away your faces.

paragraphs.text: The same over again, and yet no win repetition: Duris enim illis capitibus res non potuit satis inculcari, to these dizzards nothing could be said too much.
paragraphs.anchor: For every one of the house of Israel.

paragraphs.text: But proselyted to the Jewish religion, as Jethro, who was the first of that kind that we read of.
paragraphs.anchor: Or of the stranger.

paragraphs.text: As a harlot doth from her husband. See Hos 4:14; Hos 9:10.
paragraphs.anchor: Which separateth himself from me.

paragraphs.text: Non verbis sed verberibus; not with words, but with blows. Or, According to my most holy truth and justice; or, By myself - scil., do I swear that I will do it. See Eze 14:4.
paragraphs.anchor: I the, Lord will answer him by myself.

paragraphs.text: Vultuose torveque illum intuear. I will look him to death. Or, Laying aside all other business, I will see to it that he be soundly paid.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will set my face against that man.

paragraphs.text: That when men would express a great punishment upon any, they shall resemble it to his, as the Jews did to Ahab’s and Zedekiah’s, that naughty couple, {Jer 29:22} and the heathens to that of Tantalus {a} and Tityus.
paragraphs.anchor: And will make him a sign and a proverb.

paragraphs.text: This is yet a further and a more formidable menace; this is far worse than to he a byword to the people.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will cut him off from the midst of my people.

paragraphs.text: {a} Tantalus, q. ταλαντατος, Ut vult Plato.
I had not only a permissive, but an active hand in that imposture; not as a sin, but as a punishment of other sins. See 1Ki 22:20 Job 12:16 Jer 4:10 2Th 2:11.
paragraphs.anchor: I the Lord have deceived that prophet.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Upon that false prophet, who, although he hath thus acted, not without my providence, yet hath sinned against my law, which is the rule men must walk by, or else suffer for their transgression. Aut faciendum aut patiendum. Now God hath long hands, as we use to say of princes; neither may any think to live out of the reach of his rod.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will stretch out mine hand upon him

paragraphs.text: Neither shall excuse other; but as they have sinned together, so shall they suffer together, quia volentes et scientes errabant, they wilfully went astray. Quandoquidem hic populus vult decipi, decipiatur; they shall infallibly perish. An evil pilot may easily drown himself, and all that are with him, on the same bottom.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall bear the punishment of their iniquity.

paragraphs.text: Thus "when God’s judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness." {Isa 26:9} Those elect that were bad will become good, and they that were good will he made better. Poena ad paucos, metus ad omnes. When a few are punished, all fear.
paragraphs.anchor: That the house of Israel may go no more astray.

paragraphs.text: The utter destruction of this perverse people is once again denounced and declared to be inevitable.
paragraphs.anchor: The word of the Lord came again to me.

paragraphs.text: See on Eze 2:1.
paragraphs.anchor: Son of man.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The inhabitants of the land; not as if the land itself were alive and indued with reason, as Origen {a} doated, and as Plato held that the Spirit of God was the soul of the world.
paragraphs.anchor: When the land sinneth against me

paragraphs.text: Praevaricando perfide; by doing evil as men could.
paragraphs.anchor: By trespassing grievously.

paragraphs.text: See Eze 14:9.
paragraphs.anchor: Then will I stretch out my hand.

paragraphs.text: See Eze 4:16; Eze 5:16.
paragraphs.anchor: And will break the staff.

paragraphs.text: Extreme famine, a heavy judgment, as hath eleswhere been shown out of sacred and profane history.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will send famine.

See on Jer 15:1.
paragraphs.anchor: Though these three men.

paragraphs.text: What could not these three, so mighty with God, have done if the matter had been feasible? Daniel was now alive and in his prime; Ezekiel, his contemporary and fellow prophet, envieth him not, but celebrateth him; as also Peter doth Paul. {2Pe 3:15-16}
paragraphs.anchor: Noah, Daniel, and Job.

paragraphs.text: Because the decree was past, an end was come. {Eze 7:2; Eze 7:4-6; Eze 7:10}
paragraphs.anchor: They should deliver but their own souls.

paragraphs.text: As lions, wolves, bears, serpents, &c. Great hurt hath been done not only by such, as Num 21:6 2Ki 2:24; 2Ki 17:25-26 Jos 24:12; but also by tamer creatures when set on by God. Rebellis facta est, quia homo numini, creatura homini. {a} Rats, conies, frogs, wasps, moths, have done much mischief.
paragraphs.anchor: If I cause noisome beasts.

paragraphs.text: {a} Augustine.

All alive, and lustily tugging; yet it would not do. In common calamities heathens had their supplications and sacrifices. Papists have their litanies and processions, though to small purpose. Let us, in the like ease, up and be doing, that the Lord may be with us.
paragraphs.anchor: Though these three men were in it.

paragraphs.text: Heb., If they deliver sons, &c.; q.d., then never trust me more. Formula iurandi elliptica.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall deliver neither sons.

paragraphs.text: The sword, whensoever it comes is bathed in heaven. {Isa 34:5}
paragraphs.anchor: Or if I bring a sword.

paragraphs.text: When the sword rideth circuit, as a judge, it is in commission. See Jer 47:6-7.
paragraphs.anchor: Sword, go through the land.

paragraphs.text: {a} Though never so dear to them: τα φιλτατα, the Greeks call them.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither sons nor daughtens

Which Hippocartes calleth το Yειον, because God hath a special hand in it. Physicians can give no good reason for it.
paragraphs.anchor: Or if I send a pestilence.

paragraphs.text: i.e., In great slaughter, laying heaps upon heaps.
paragraphs.anchor: In blood

paragraphs.text: Though it were an only one, and so more dear to them.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither son nor daughter.

paragraphs.anchor: They shall but deliver.

paragraphs.text: Every one of the four (Cardan reckons three more of like nature, viz., earthquakes, inundations, and great winds) are sore judgments indeed. Each of them is pessimum, most wicked, i.e., perniciosum. Cavete. Dangerous. Beware.
paragraphs.anchor: My four sore judgments.
